summary: Shared checkpoints are removed: members no longer seal, verify, excuse or adopt checkpoints, and every member trims its own copy by default with the local trim planner ([trim] local = true; local = false turns it off). Retired claim IDs still travel to peers, which never admit, ask for or serve them again

replay.detail: No replay. Claims, positions, projections and tombstones are untouched; a cut a member had already committed (`trimming`) finishes as before, and a shared checkpoint it was still recording is forgotten without deleting anything.

schema.detail: No table, column or storage version change. The checkpoint tables, retired ledgers and capture guard keep their layout. checkpoint.sealed, checkpoint.verified and checkpoint.excused stay registered and admitted, since old history and older members carry them, but this build writes no new ones.

rules.detail: Trimming is on by default on every member: each day a member plans its own due cut with the existing audited rules and guards (dropping only LOCAL_TRIM_KINDS: observer.observed, harness.observed and resource.observed) and deletes at most [trim] daily_claims claims (100,000 unless set). There is no fleet barrier, agreement or proof copy; a plan that would drop the newest claim of a subject and kind, or a delete that would change the graph, stops the trim with a local-trim-stopped fault until `fractal replication checkpoint resume` is run. The [checkpoint] section still loads but is ignored, and the daemon logs "[checkpoint] is ignored: every member trims on its own ([trim])".

compatibility.detail: An older member that still runs shared checkpoints counts this member as a participant, and this member never seals, so the older member's shared checkpoints stop becoming stable, as they do today for any [trim] local member; after a few days the older member asks a person to excuse this member. This build advertises no checkpoint in its inventory, so an older member adopts nothing from it. The internal checkpoint manifest routes (/v1/internal/replication/checkpoint*, /v1/checkpoint*) and the `fractal replication checkpoint plan`, `status` and `excuse` commands are removed; `fractal replication checkpoint resume` stays. Retired claim IDs travel only between members that trim locally; an older ordinary member neither sends nor reads them, and this member refuses the claims it retired from any peer. Members that trim retain the same claims apart from those some member retired: a copy a peer holds stays until its own trim drops it, so the claim_sources and operations projection digests of two members can differ until retired IDs also delete held copies (#6878, a later release).

downtime.detail: No startup work. A member that did not trim locally before becomes the retired ledger's authority once its existing background import has finished, then trims its first due cut on the normal ten-minute step, paced and capped at [trim] daily_claims a day.

manual.detail: On each older member that still runs shared checkpoints, a person either upgrades it or runs `fractal replication checkpoint excuse NAME --reason TEXT --as person/NAME` there (the command exists on older builds) for each member running this build, so the older members' shared checkpoints can become stable again. Nothing is needed on members running this build. A member that should keep everything sets [trim] local = false. Before rolling a member back to the previous release, set [trim] local = true explicitly in its config (this build omits the default line and the previous release defaults to false); otherwise the rolled-back member may re-admit claims this build retired from a peer that still holds them.

recovery.detail: Rollback to the previous release is supported. Its shared checkpoints resume waiting for agreement. What this build trimmed stays trimmed, but retired claims stay retired only while that release has [trim] local = true, which its config must then say explicitly (this build omits the default line, and the previous release defaults to false); otherwise its admission reads the checkpoint tables rather than the retired ledger, and a claim this build retired may be re-admitted from a peer that still holds it. That costs space only: the claims were dropped because a kept claim answers every reader the same.
